metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Our results for selfing thus far have only been concerned with selection among lines. If selection is practiced entirely within a single selfed lineage (e.g., within the progeny of a single selfed individual), genetic variation is quickly removed and the selection response rapidly ceases. Pederson (1969b) obtained the response remaining in generation T from within-family selection in generation t as [[SEE_FORMULA:23.42a]] where $ \sigma_{E_{w}}^{2} $ is the within-family environmental variance among individuals. Because any within-family genetic variation rapidly decays, after only a few generations the response essentially stops, with the amount of permanent response due to selection in generation $ t $ depending on $ \sigma_A^2 / 2^t $. Because [[SEE_FORMULA:23.43a]] it follows that the permanent response $ (T \to \infty) $ can be bounded by noting [[SEE_FORMULA:23.43b]] Because the leftmost and rightmost power series sum to one, the total permanent response $ R(\infty \mid \infty) $ under continued within-family selection (ignoring new mutation) is [[SEE_FORMULA:23.43c]] showing that the total response is at least twice the response of the first generation ($ \bar{\imath}h\sigma_{A}/2 $).
